items.title: Donald Trump Has Already Benefitted from “Spoiler” Candidates Aided by Republican Lawyers and More
items.author: Lisa Graves
items.content:
With all the controversy swirling around the U.S. Senate race in Alaska, an important piece of context has been largely absent from the coverage of Democrat Mary Peltola’s bid to unseat Republican Sen. Dan S. Sullivan: Donald Trump has been the beneficiary of numerous “spoiler” candidates and initiatives aiding his political ambitions.

This month, Trump directed the Justice Department to try to halt the election underway, citing Republican objections to the candidacy of Dan J. Sullivan, Jr., a potential spoiler to the GOP. But the Alaska Supreme Court already ruled that removing Dan J. Sullivan from the ballot would be unlawful. Plus, the ballot makes clear that Dan S. Sullivan is the “registered Republican” and the “incumbent,” while the other Dan Sullivan is not.

Trump’s unprecedented intervention could determine whether his political party remains in control of the Senate and able to rubber stamp the operatives he wants installed as judges and government officials, like his lickspittle personal lawyer, Todd Blanche, who is now paid by us to act as the Attorney General of the United States.

Long-standing DOJ rules and policies have prevented the use of prosecutorial power close to–and specifically before–elections to avoid government interference in the democratic process… until now. Under Trump, that restraint has effectively disappeared.

Blanche’s selective use of prosecutorial power is also evinced by the way he has gone after Trump’s political targets, like James Comey, who, as FBI director, refused to swear a loyalty oath to Trump in 2017. Blanche is pursuing criminal charges against him for a third time, now accusing him of leaking national security information in 2016.

Speaking of Russia, the hypocrisy is striking. Trump is hammering Peltola for purportedly “stacking” the race with a candidate who has the same name as her opponent to siphon off votes. But Trump himself sought to stack the deck against his 2016 political opponent Hillary Clinton by literally inviting Russia, a foreign adversary, to help him out. “Russia, if you’re listening,” Trump infamously declared, urging Moscow to find the 30,000 emails allegedly missing from Clinton’s private server. Russia went on to interfere in the election in numerous ways and helped Trump win.

Afterward, his son-in-law Jared Kushner, with Kislyak’s help, even sought to set up a secret phone line with Russia at a diplomatic facility in DC to shield his communications with Vladimir Putin from the U.S. intelligence community. In the years since then, Trump has repeatedly acted like Putin’s stooge, destroying American foreign policy and alienating our nation’s closest strategic allies by acting in alignment with Putin’s interests. Todd Blanche has taken no action to investigate any of it.

That’s not the only way Trump has benefited from spoilers in elections, even leaving aside his mysterious admissions about his billionaire buddy Elon Musk’s 2024 actions: “He knows those computers better than anybody. All those computers. Those vote-counting computers ... And we ended up winning Pennsylvania like in a landslide.” Blanche is not investigating that either.

Among those helping her in 2024 was Jay Sekulow, a right-wing lawyer who represented Trump in his first impeachment trial. Sekulow is also known as one of the “four horsemen”–alongside Leonard Leo and two others–who helped get John Roberts and Samuel Alito installed on the U.S. Supreme Court. Does anyone seriously believe that Sekulow, a Trump loyalist, would help Stein if doing so didn’t benefit his man?

Stein, like Dan J. Sullivan, had a right to run–even though her campaign was never designed to actually win the election. It was meant to draw votes away from Democrats. In 2024, she was especially focused on targeting Muslim Americans, many of whom were angry over the Biden administration’s aid to Israel in the war killing civilians in Gaza.

Stein also paid $100,000 to a Republican-tied firm called “Accelevate,” led by Trent Pool, who, according to , was reportedly inside the Capitol with a Gadsden flag on January 6. And Stein was not Pool’s only 2024 client. His firm also received at least $10 million from the campaign of Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., who was running as an “independent” to siphon off “MAHA” moms from the Democratic Party. He eventually dropped out to endorse Trump–who rewarded him with a key cabinet position.

In 2020, Kanye “Ye” West took off his red MAGA hat to announce an independent campaign for president. As with Stein and RFK, Jr., major Republican players worked to get him on the ballot, positioning him to draw some Black votes away from Biden/Harris. As the Daily Beast reported: West’s 2020 campaign “appears to have disguised potentially millions of dollars in services it received from a secretive network of Republican Party operatives, including advisers to the GOP elite and a managing partner at one of the top conservative political firms in the country.”

Before Trump’s rise to power in 2016, billionaires Charles and David Koch were also busy promoting potential spoiler candidates to counter President Barack Obama, whom Trump had been assailing over his birth certificate since 2011. In 2011-2012, they used Tea Party events organized by the Koch-funded Americans for Prosperity to promote Herman Cain’s presidential campaign, which was run by one of the Kochs’ long-time operatives in Wisconsin, to potentially siphon away some Black voters. Years later, Cain backed Trump and remained an avid supporter until he died from Covid-19 in 2020.

So, here we are in 2026, with Trump wielding the power of the U.S. Department of Justice to accuse a Democratic Senate candidate and her staff of taking a page from his own party’s playbook. Peltola, meanwhile, has denied being part of the ballot-stacking effort.

Truth be told, the strategy of using candidates with similar names to draw votes away from opponents is hardly new in American politics. Both parties and their allies have employed variations of the vote syphoning tactic for decades. It’s not pretty, but it’s the way politics has been played repeatedly, and there’s no proof that any of what has been alleged–and denied–in the Alaska Senate race violates the law.

But there have been criminal efforts to interfere in our elections–by Donald Trump. So let’s remember just who is pushing for a criminal investigation in Alaska: the felon president, the king of modern election interference and subversion.

items.title: GOP Now Stands for “Gang of Predators”
items.author: Lisa Graves
items.content:
It is both shocking and totally on brand for Donald Trump and JD Vance to defend Vivek Ramaswamy’s vile, million-dollar ad campaign weaponizing a child molester’s wife to attack Dr. Amy Acton, his opponent in Ohio’s gubernatorial race.

He continued to sexually abuse her until he was arrested when she was 12. The state took Amy and her little brother, Phil Stearns, away from Donna and Cledith. Phil stands by his sister, noting that Donna “stayed married to Amy’s rapist until he died” in 2004.

Back in 1974, the year before he married Donna, Cledith Arthur had been charged with “incest” of a different child. That charge was two years before he began raping Amy.

That’s not all that is relevant and totally appalling.

In 1996, Donna Arthur–going by the last name “Hollopeter”--was found guilty of felony theft and passing bad checks. That is, the woman who Ramaswamy has lifted up to call her daughter a “liar” was literally convicted of the crime of “theft by deception,” which is stealing by lying. Donna–who lost custody of her children for neglect and for not protecting her daughter from a sexual predator–was charged with animal neglect, too, just five years ago in 2021.

You cannot make up such wretchedness.

In any sane universe, a candidate for governor would never run an ad featuring a child molester’s lover, a woman complicit in his abuse and also his after-the-fact accomplice.

Vivek’s action in taking her side is utter depravity.

Sure, Cledith Arthur pleaded “not guilty” before jumping bond and fleeing Ohio for Pennsylvania with his wife. Their flight from justice prevented a trial and his conviction as a monstrous pedophile, but I consider his evasion to be more evidence of his guilt.

And I will not call that woman Amy’s “mother” or “mom.” In my opinion, she forfeited that title when she betrayed her young daughter instead of protecting her from the predator she had invited into their lives. Now she has wormed her way out of the shadows to harm Amy, again, this time with the help of Vivek and his enormous wealth. There is a special place in hell for such betrayers of their sacred parental duty, like Alice Munro.

In any normal timeline, a candidate’s top advisors would resign if their boss insisted on running an attack ad siding with a child molester and his lover against the child who survived such horrifying abuse. Instead, Vivek’s spokesperson, Connie Luck, defended the ad and again attacked Dr. Acton’s character. That’s shameless, and I have a right to wish that Luck never has the good luck to get a good job ever again.

In any healthy administration, the president and the vice president would condemn the ad, urge Ramaswamy to take it down, and call on him to step down from the race.

But this is not a healthy administration. It is deeply unwell. It is morally sick.

I say this all in my personal capacity, not on behalf of any organization. Trump is wicked, a magnet of corruption, who attracts and collects the iron filings of men and women willing to trade their integrity for power, wealth, and fame—people like JD Vance.

Vance should have been unwelcome back in Ohio after telling foul lies about innocent, hard-working Haitian immigrants living in the state in 2024. After his defense of Vivek’s ad, Vance should be disowned by the state.

Despite his own track record, Vance—a recent Catholic convert—had the audacity this summer to try to lecture the Pope on Catholic tenets after Pope Leo rebuked the warmongering of Trump and Vance. Vance even published a memoir this year telling his tales about “finding my way back to faith,” a faith that includes the Ten Commandments, which expressly condemns bearing false witness. This week, rather than denounce Vivek’s ad featuring the child molester’s paramour, Vance assailed Acton’s character and dismissed any Republican critics, telling them to “stop whining.”

Vance should be ashamed. Instead, he is doubling down.

This would all be bad enough… but there’s more.

The Republicans installed a man who continues to act like Donald Trump’s personal defense attorney as Attorney General of the United States. That man, Todd Blanche, has expressed more sympathy for convicted sex trafficker Ghislaine Maxwell than for the victims and survivors of her schemes with Jeffrey Epstein. To this day, under Blanche’s direction, numerous Epstein-related records mentioning Donald Trump remain hidden. On Blanche’s watch, Maxwell was moved to a country club prison camp with more lenient conditions, and DOJ is investigating none of the other men named in the Epstein files.

His Secretary of Defense, Pete Hegseth, was accused of raping a woman, who said she suspected he roofied her. Hegseth denied the claim before ultimately settling the case.

Trump’s Supreme Court nominee Brett Kavanaugh also faced an accusation of sexual assault from his former classmate, Dr. Christine Blasey Ford. He bombastically denied it and was confirmed to the nation’s highest court with Sen. Susan Collins (R-ME) casting a pivotal vote in his favor, alongside nearly every other Republican senator.

Kavanaugh joined a Supreme Court where Republicans had previously installed Clarence Thomas, who was accused of repeatedly sexually harassing a woman who had worked for him. Thomas loudly denied the allegations too, but I found Anita Hill’s testimony compelling, just like Ford’s.

And this is only a partial accounting of the rot involving GOP men accused of sexual predators. Then there are the high profile men, like Ramaswamy and Vance, actively men credibly accused of rape, including the rape of children, as with Amy Acton’s case.

As I have said repeatedly since 2018, when Trump and his loyalist Republicans jammed Kavanaugh onto the Supreme Court (though he should have been impeached from the judiciary instead), America does not face a crisis of false accusations by women and girls. Most cases of rape are never reported. The real problem is false denials.

We have an epidemic of false denials.

That is partly because men accused of rape lie and deny that they did anything wrong.

And, in America, those who are accused have the right to plead not guilty, whether they are guilty or not, and face a trial with their neighbors as jurors. While most of those charges for sexual assault result in convictions or guilty pleas, we do not make an accounting of just how many of those men made false denials from the outset. Rarely do such trials result in acquittals or hung juries, but it sometimes happens after the defense tries to put the accuser on trial, scrutinizing what they wore, what they drank, or how they behaved.

Rarer still are the cases in which a man accused of molesting a child becomes a fugitive from justice, like the predator Donna Arthur repeatedly chose over her only daughter.

I hope justice prevails and the guy fueling these attacks–who I am going to call “Vivek Reallyslimy” from here on out–loses big time.

People of integrity and good conscience must take a stand against the dirtiest of dirty politics that he, Trump, and Vance are playing here.

I really hope a giant wave of justice breaks through and politically wipes out those who defend rapists and pedophiles and their enablers. And, I hope that wave also washes out any candidate for any office anywhere who refuses to condemn Reallyslimy’s ad and does not call on him to step down from the race.

The rest of us have had enough of this wickedness.

The time for accountability is well past due.

    • This book was written by two heroes of mine shortly after Thomas was installed on the Supreme Court. Jane and Jill are such excellent investigative reporters and writers. I look forward to their newest works.
